description:
One-Time Ticket — a complete OctoMesh demo app in a single installable bundle.
Staging/production channel variant (mirrors System.Communication.Release).

A developer creates a "ticket" holding a secret (e.g. an API key) and shares a
redeem link. The secret can be fetched over HTTP exactly once; afterwards the
ticket is burned (redeemed flag set, secret cleared in the data mesh).
The secret is a Secret attribute (Demo.Tickets 1.3.0): stored encrypted, never
returned by queries; only the redeem pipeline reveals it (RevealSecret@1).

What this blueprint installs:
- the Demo.Tickets construction kit model (auto-imported from the catalog)
- a DataFlow with 3 HTTP pipelines hosted by the tenant's Mesh Adapter:
    POST /tickets   create a ticket  -> { ticketId }
    GET  /tickets   list tickets     -> { tickets: [...] } (never the secret)
    GET  /redeem    ?id=<ticketId>   -> { secret } once, then { error }
- the One-Time Ticket web app as an Application workload, rolled out to
  Kubernetes by the Communication Operator as a Helm release, pulling the
  one-time-ticket-app chart from the meshmakers-apps release Helm repo.

PREREQUISITE: communication must be enabled on the target tenant. The
service-managed System.Communication.Release blueprint seeds the deployment site
(670000000000000000000001), Mesh Adapter (670000000000000000000002) and the
apps release Helm repo (670000000000000000000005) this seed associates to.
We point at that pre-seeded repo rather than seeding our own.

Install only seeds entities — trigger the rollout afterwards with
DeployDataFlow (the pipelines) + DeployWorkload (the web app).
UPGRADE from 2.0.x: redeploy the DataFlow right after installing this version
(the redeem pipeline uses RevealSecret@1, which needs the Secret model). The
redeem route is anonymous, so RevealSecret@1 runs as the Mesh Adapter's service
account; that account must be allowed to read Demo.Tickets/Ticket.

NOTE: the dev/test variant is OneTimeTicket.MainLatest. Keep the seed-data of
the two variants in sync — they differ only in the Application's HelmRepository
association (003 dev vs 005 apps).
